notes.안녕하세요, 전현상입니다. 오늘은 작은 모델 하나를 튜닝하고 INT4로: Hello, I'm Hyeonsang Jeon. Today I'll share the results of an experiment I ran myself: tuning one small model, shrinking it to INT4, and serving it with vLLM. Every number comes from the same model, the same questions and the same GPU. I'll talk about what worked and what didn't, and also about what this experiment cannot tell us.
notes.작은 모델을 튜닝해서 서비스에 쓰려면 궁금한 게 세 가지 있어요. 튜닝하: If you want to tune a small model and use it in a service, there are three things you want to know. How much does tuning improve it, how much does it lose when you shrink it, and what are the speed and cost when you serve it? I'll answer these three questions in this order: training, quantization, serving and cost. Every answer is a number measured with the same model, questions and GPU.
notes.모델은 KT가 공개한 Mi:dm 2.0 Base, 11.5B입니다. 데이: The model is Mi:dm 2.0 Base, 11.5B, an open model from KT. The data is KorMedMCQA. These are past questions from the national licensing exams for doctors, nurses, pharmacists and dentists. We trained on the 2012-2020 questions and used the 2021 questions only for a dev check. Final accuracy was measured on 3,009 questions from 2022-2024, only once per model. The hardware is one H100 NVL, and there is a single seed, 42.
notes.실제 문항으로 간호사 국가시험 2019년 1교시 1번을 가져왔습니다. 보: Here is a real question: question 1 of session 1 of the 2019 nurse licensing exam. The model was asked to answer with just the number of the correct option. During training, loss is applied only to two tokens: the answer number and the token that closes the turn. In front of the actual request, the Mi:dm template adds its fixed system text, about 450 tokens. This text comes back later, together with prefix caching.
notes.정답률은 2022~2024년 3,009문항 기준이에요. 튜닝 전 63.3: Accuracy is on the 3,009 questions from 2022-2024. The untuned model's 63.3% became 72.3% after LoRA training. The model trained with Unsloth is the same, at 72.2%. Shrinking to INT4 brings it down to 69.5% for PTQ and 69.7% for QAT. Both are still above the 60% reference pass line. All of these numbers were measured with a single seed on one H100.
notes.첫 번째는 학습입니다. 같은 LoRA 학습을 transformers+PE: First, training. We ran the same LoRA training with transformers+PEFT and with Unsloth, and compare how training time, GPU memory and accuracy change when only the engine changes.
notes.바꾼 것은 학습 엔진 하나입니다. 한쪽은 transformers Trai: The only thing we changed is the training engine. One side is the transformers Trainer with PEFT, the other is Unsloth. Data, LoRA settings, training schedule, seed and GPU were kept the same. Gradient checkpointing, though, used each engine's own method. After training, both merge the LoRA and save a single BF16 model.
Training for 426 steps went from 24.3 minutes to 15.7 minutes, 35% less. Memory as seen by nvidia-smi went from 82.3 to 25.5 GiB. That is a single reading at one point in time, so it is not the peak. Accuracy was 72.3% and 72.2%, p=0.89, so no difference. The gradient checkpointing methods differ, so part of the difference may come from that setting, and the torch versions also differ. This result was measured with a single seed on one GPU type.
notes.직접 해 보실 분께 드리는 이야기예요. Mi:dm 2.0을 Unsloth: This one is for those of you who want to try it yourselves. If you load Mi:dm 2.0 as is with Unsloth 2026.11.3, it stops at the tokenizer. First, pin transformers to 4.57.6. Even then, importing unsloth while a GPU is visible breaks it again. So we read the tokenizer in a separate process that had not loaded Unsloth, and passed it in. We did not find the patch that causes this.
notes.두 번째는 모델을 줄이는 일입니다. 도구는 TorchAO, 토치 에이오예: Second, shrinking the model. The tool is TorchAO, said "torch A-O". It is a quantization library made by the PyTorch team, and AO is short for Architecture Optimization. It has tools that shrink weights to low bit widths such as INT4, and QAT tools that train the model to prepare it for being shrunk. With it, we shrink the BF16 LoRA model to INT4 and measure how much accuracy PTQ and QAT lose.
notes.INT4는 가중치 하나를 16개 값 중 하나로 반올림해 저장합니다. PT: INT4 stores each weight rounded to one of 16 values. PTQ rounds the trained model as it is. There is no training, so it is done in 17 seconds, but the rounding error stays. QAT makes the model compute with already-rounded values during training. The model experiences that error and adjusts its weights. It is like practicing with the real equipment on, and it took 1 hour 42 minutes for 600 steps. The difference from training more on the same data is also part of this comparison. In both, only the weights are INT4, and computation is in BF16.
notes.INT4로 바꾸면 크기가 21.51에서 7.20 GiB, 3분의 1이 됩: Converting to INT4 takes the size from 21.51 to 7.20 GiB, down to 1/3. Accuracy went down 2.9 percentage points for PTQ and 2.6 points for QAT. We paired the questions one by one and ran a McNemar test. The result is that both differences are hard to attribute to chance. Even so, both INT4 models are more than 6 points above the untuned model. These numbers also come from a single seed.
notes.이 실행에서 QAT는 PTQ보다 0.2%p 높았습니다. 다시 학습하거나: In this run, QAT was 0.2 percentage points above PTQ. When we retrained or changed the seed and compared six times, QAT was 0.2 to 1.0 points higher every time. But that difference is about the size of the error that comes from the questions, so we cannot decide whether it is better. How much accuracy dropped differs by profession. Dentist dropped by only 0.7 to 1.2 points. There is only a single QAT setting: learning rate 1e-5, 600 steps.
notes.세 번째는 서빙입니다. 요청 수와 prefix caching에 따라 BF: Third, serving. We find out which is faster, BF16 or INT4, depending on the number of requests and on prefix caching. Both models were served with vLLM.
notes.서빙 속도는 두 가지로 쟀습니다. 오프라인에서는 요청 1~256개를 GP: We measured serving speed in two ways. Offline, we put 1 to 256 requests into the GPU at once and looked at throughput. Online, what we looked at was response time. That is the case where several users ask an OpenAI-compatible server at the same time. INT4 PTQ and QAT have the same format, so their throughput is within 1%. So online, we measured PTQ only.
notes.오프라인에서 한 번에 넣은 요청이 1~4개면 INT4가 20% 안팎 빠릅: Offline, with 1 to 4 requests at once, INT4 is about 20% faster. For one request to receive all 128 tokens, BF16 takes 1.10 seconds and INT4 takes 0.70 seconds. With 16 or more requests BF16 is ahead, and at 256 the gap is 9 times. INT4 stops in the 800s of tokens per second. The measurements used one GPU type, H100.
notes.이 서비스는 프롬프트가 약 650토큰이고 답은 숫자 하나죠. 그래서 거의: In this service, the prompt is about 650 tokens and the answer is a single number. So almost all of the time goes to prompt processing. We sent new questions at each concurrency level, so only the prefix shared by every request was reused from the cache. With prefix caching on, INT4 gets 4 to 6 times faster, and time to first token went from 542 to 110 ms. Even so, at concurrency 8 and above, BF16 handles about 3 times as many, even with caching on. INT4 with caching off is stuck at 2 requests per second.
notes.답이 긴 대화형 경우도 봤어요. 128토큰을 생성하면 요청 하나일 때 I: We also looked at the chat-style case with long answers. When generating 128 tokens with a single request, INT4 does 180 tokens per second, faster than BF16's 116. With 8 or more concurrent requests BF16 is ahead, and at 64 it is 3,541 vs 1,025 tokens. The prompts were already in the cache, so please read this as a table that compares generation speed only.
notes.왜 이렇게 갈리는지 짚어 볼게요. 요청이 적으면 가중치를 메모리에서 읽는: Let me go over why it splits this way. With few requests, most of the time goes to reading weights from memory. So INT4, whose weights are 1/3 the size, has the advantage. With many requests, computation becomes the bottleneck. BF16 uses tensor-core matrix multiplication as is, while tile-packed INT4 computes through the tinygemm kernel, which unpacks the weights as it goes. We did not do kernel-level profiling, so this explanation is a hypothesis.
notes.마지막은 비용이에요. 자체 GPU 비용을 먼저 봅니다. 그다음 같은 문항: Last, cost. First we look at the cost on a self-hosted GPU. Then we have 11 managed API models answer the same questions, and put accuracy and cost side by side.
notes.비용은 계산으로 낸 값인데요. 잰 시간과 처리량에 H100 온디맨드 정가: These costs are calculated values. We multiplied the measured time and throughput by the H100 on-demand list price, $6.98 per hour. When all 3,009 questions are run at once, BF16 is 15 times cheaper than INT4. Through a server at concurrency 64, INT4 costs $1.023 per 1,000 questions with prefix caching off, and $0.175 with it on. BF16 at concurrency 64 with prefix caching on costs $0.059 per 1,000 questions. These values assume the server is busy without a break. We compare with managed APIs on the next slide.
notes.같은 3,009문항을 매니지드 API 모델 11개에도 풀게 했어요. 10: We also had 11 managed API models answer the same 3,009 questions. 10 of them were more accurate than the tuned Mi:dm, and the highest model scored 98.4%. When all 3,009 questions are run at once, the self-hosted GPU is the cheapest, but on a server that takes one request at a time, some APIs are both cheaper and more accurate. The API models either have undisclosed sizes or are much larger, and their training data is unknown.
notes.API와 차이가 컸거든요. 그래서 다른 모델의 출력 없이 Mi:dm 점수: The gap with the APIs was large. So we measured separately whether Mi:dm's score could be raised further without other models' outputs. Besides epochs and learning rate, we shuffled the option order, which also changes the answer number. We showed the professions with fewer questions more often. We also trained on explanations from the untuned Mi:dm, on questions it got right 2 or more times out of 4. No experiment passed the bar. Changing only the seed moved the score by 0.9 to 1.5 percentage points, and every difference was within that.
notes.네 줄로 정리할게요. Unsloth로 같은 LoRA 학습을 24.3분에서: Let me sum up in four lines. With Unsloth, the same LoRA training went from 24.3 minutes to 15.7 minutes, and accuracy stayed the same. The model shrunk to INT4 with TorchAO is 1/3 the size and lost 2.6 to 2.9 percentage points of accuracy. QAT was a little higher than PTQ, but we could not decide whether it is better. In serving, which one is faster flips with the number of requests. When requests pile up, BF16 is ahead. Most APIs were more accurate, and when everything was run at once, the self-hosted GPU was the cheapest.
notes.이 숫자로는 말할 수 없는 것도 있어요. seed는 42 하나이고 see: There are also things these numbers cannot tell us. There is a single seed, 42, and changing only the seed moves the score by about 1 percentage point. There is one GPU type, H100, and only a single QAT setting and a single INT4 scheme. For prefix caching, we measured only the case where the shared prefix is reused. In the managed API comparison, the cost bases differ, and the API models' training data is unknown. Next, I plan to measure again with a different INT4 kernel.
notes.코드와 결과 JSON, 따라 하는 방법은 GitHub에 모두 공개했습니다: The code, the result JSONs and the step-by-step guide are all public on GitHub. Without a GPU, you can check in 1 minute that this repo works. What it checks: the tests, the doc numbers against the result JSONs, and redrawing the charts. The trained models are published on Hugging Face and may be used for non-commercial purposes only. They are not models for medical advice. I'll take your questions now. Thank you.
